text:
maya: Heads-up — I'm drafting a PRD for generation edge cases around streaming/truncation/token limits/retries. Need acceptance criteria + launch checklist. Can we align on scope today?

darren: thanks maya. quick q — is the ask to change API surface or just to tighten behavior for existing streaming endpoints?

maya: keep surface same for now. focus on deterministic semantics: when we stream partial tokens, how do we signal truncation vs finalization, and what's the retry contract for clients.

li: main runtime constraints: KV cache size, prefix caching, and sequence length vs memory. We'll need clear failure modes so runtime can map to fallback strategies.

emma: customers seeing silent truncation in some long-context flows (legal doc ingestion). they want a flag so they can detect truncation reliably and retry upstream.

greg: from UX: prefer explicit event types in stream: `data`, `truncated`, `complete`, `error`. visual clients can then show a banner if truncated.

darren: acceptance criteria proposal: 1) every streamed session must end with either `complete` or `truncated` event; 2) a `truncated` event includes truncated_token_count and a reason code (e.g., input_limit, output_limit, safety_truncate); 3) retries only allowed if last event was `error` or runtime transient, not after `truncated` unless client increments prompt or changes params.

li: add: token accounting must be deterministic across retries to avoid double-billing surprises — include request_id and an idempotency_token in events.

maya: good. also need SLOs: under 95th percentile latency target for first-byte 150ms on hosted; fallback model policy must not increase client-observed order anomalies.

darren: edge-case enumeration we should cover in PRD: 
- mid-stream runtime OOM -> emit `error` with code `OOM_RUNTIME` and best-effort partial.
- network disconnect -> client reconnect semantics + resume? we currently don't support resume; must be explicit in docs.
- token-limit reached (output) -> emit `truncated`.
- input too long -> reject early with helpful payload.

emma: customers want guidance: when to retry vs when to restart with higher token budget. we should add suggested retry/backoff pattern in SDKs.

greg: acceptance test ideas: synthetic replay harness that simulates disconnects and OOMs, asserts final event and metrics emitted.

maya: launch criteria draft: 1) PRD + RFC reviewed by eng/runtime, devex, legal (for safety truncation message); 2) unit + integration tests green; 3) e2e test with 3 pilot customers confirming truncation flag works; 4) observability: new metrics (truncation_count, resume_attempts, stream_error_rate) in console; 5) docs + SDK examples updated.

li: implementation risks: resume semantics are nontrivial (KV cache state + ordering). recommend we don't promise resume in this release; document as future work.

darren: scope negotiation note: we can do deterministic signaling (events & codes) + billing idempotency in v1. Resume/partial-resume in v2.

maya: agreed. prioritization: v1 = deterministic end events + clear error codes + SDK examples + tests + telemetry. v2 = resume, advanced backpressure APIs, adaptive truncation.

emma: i'll line up 3 pilot customers who reported this with clear test prompts. we'll ask them to validate logs and truncation flags.

greg: small UX ask: add short copy example for truncated banner and one-liner for error UI in docs.

maya: next steps: I'll put PRD draft in drive and file RFC. @darren @li please add acceptance criteria comments inline. I'll schedule a 30m sync tomorrow to finalize launch checklist.

deploy-bot: canary plan note: when ready, plan a 10% canary for 48h, monitor `truncated_rate` and `stream_error_rate` before wider rollout.

darren: noted. I'll start a spike on idempotency headers and event schema.

maya: thanks team — aim to have RFC ready for review by EOD tomorrow. :rocket:
